post.description:
Accepts a certificate enrollment request and begins processing it.

Allowed private key types:
- RSA (OID: 1.2.840.113549.1.1.1), key length equal to 2048 bits,
- EC (elliptic curve-based keys, OID: 1.2.840.10045.2.1), NIST P-256 curve (secp256r1)

The use of EC keys is recommended.

Allowed signature algorithms:
- RSA PKCS#1 v1.5,
- RSA PSS,
- ECDSA (signature format compliant with RFC 3279)

Allowed hash functions used for CSR signing:
- SHA1,
- SHA256,
- SHA384,
- SHA512

> More information:
> - [Submitting a certificate enrollment request](https://github.com/CIRFMF/ksef-docs/blob/main/certyfikaty-KSeF.md#4-wys%C5%82anie-wniosku-certyfikacyjnego)

post.summary: Grant permissions to natural persons to work in KSeF
post.description:
The method allows granting permissions to work in KSeF to the person indicated in the request  
in the current context.
            
The request specifies the permissions to be granted from the following set:  
- **InvoiceWrite** – issuing invoices,  
- **InvoiceRead** – viewing invoices,  
- **CredentialsManage** – managing permissions,  
- **CredentialsRead** – viewing permissions,  
- **Introspection** – viewing session history and generating UPO,  
- **SubunitManage** – managing subordinate units,  
- **EnforcementOperations** – performing enforcement operations.
            
The method allows selecting any combination of the above permissions.  
The **EnforcementOperations** permission can only be granted when  
the context subject has the role of **EnforcementAuthority** (enforcement authority)  
or **CourtBailiff** (court bailiff).

> More information:
> - [Granting permissions](https://github.com/CIRFMF/ksef-docs/blob/main/uprawnienia.md#nadawanie-uprawnie%C5%84-osobom-fizycznym-do-pracy-w-ksef)

post.description:
The method allows granting administrator permissions to the entity or natural person indicated in the request, in the context of:
- the NIP of the indicated subordinate entity – exclusively if the entity of the current login context has the role of a parent entity:
  - **LocalGovernmentUnit**
  - **VatGroupUnit**
- the indicated or created internal identifier

When a subordinate unit administrator is created, an internal identifier is created consisting of the NIP of the login context entity and 5 digits that uniquely identify the internal unit.
The last digit must be a valid check digit, which is calculated according to the algorithm below.

The algorithm uses alternating weights (1×, 3×, 1×, 3×, ...), sums the results and returns the remainder of division by 10.

Example:
- Input: "6824515772-1234" (without check digit)
- Position 0 (1st digit): 6 × 1 = 6
- Position 1 (2nd digit): 8 × 3 = 24
- Position 2 (3rd digit): 2 × 1 = 2
- Position 3 (4th digit): 4 × 3 = 12
- Position 4 (5th digit): 5 × 1 = 5
- Position 5 (6th digit): 1 × 3 = 3
- Position 6 (7th digit): 5 × 1 = 5
- Position 7 (8th digit): 7 × 3 = 21
- Position 8 (9th digit): 7 × 1 = 7
- Position 9 (10th digit): 2 × 3 = 6
- Position 10 (11th digit): 1 × 1 = 1
- Position 11 (12th digit): 2 × 3 = 6
- Position 12 (13th digit): 3 × 1 = 3

post.summary: Retrieving the list of own permissions
post.description:
This method allows the authenticated API client to read their own permissions in the current login context.  

 The response includes the following permissions:  
 - granted directly in the current context  
 - granted by the parent entity  
 - granted indirectly, if the entity of the login context is an intermediary or target entity in the permission  
 - granted to an entity for invoice handling by another entity, if the authenticated entity has ownership permissions in the current context  

 Permissions returned by the operation include:  
 - **CredentialsManage** – managing permissions  
 - **CredentialsRead** – viewing permissions  
 - **InvoiceWrite** – issuing invoices  
 - **InvoiceRead** – viewing invoices  
 - **Introspection** – viewing session history  
 - **SubunitManage** – managing subunits  
 - **EnforcementOperations** – performing enforcement operations  
 - **VatEuManage** – managing permissions within a EU entity  

 The response can be filtered based on the following parameters:  
 - **contextIdentifier** – identifier of the entity that granted the invoice handling permission  
 - **targetIdentifier** – identifier of the target entity for indirectly granted permissions  
 - **permissionTypes** – list of permission types to search for  
 - **permissionState** – permission status  

#### Result pagination
The query returns **one page of results** with the number and size specified in the path.
- On the first call, set the parameter `pageOffset = 0`.  
- If another page of results is available, the **`hasMore`** flag will appear in the response.  
- In that case, the query can be called again with the next page number.

post.summary: Retrieving the list of KSeF permissions granted to natural persons or entities
post.description:
This method allows reading permissions granted to a natural person or entity.  
 The list of retrieved permissions can be of two types:  
 - A list of all permissions applicable in the current login context (used when an administrator wants to review the permissions of all users in the current context)  
 - A list of all permissions granted in the current context by the authenticated API client (used when an administrator wants to review the list of permissions they have granted in the current context)  

 For the first list (applicable permissions), the response includes:  
 - persons and entities able to work in the current context, except for persons authorized indirectly  
 - persons authorized indirectly by the entity of the current context  

 For the second list (granted permissions), the response includes:  
 - permissions granted directly to work in the current context or in the context of subunits  
 - permissions granted indirectly to handle clients of the current context entity  

 Permissions returned by the operation include:  
 - **CredentialsManage** – managing permissions  
 - **CredentialsRead** – viewing permissions  
 - **InvoiceWrite** – issuing invoices  
 - **InvoiceRead** – viewing invoices  
 - **Introspection** – viewing session history  
 - **SubunitManage** – managing subunits  
 - **EnforcementOperations** – performing enforcement operations  

 The response can be filtered based on the following parameters:  
 - **authorIdentifier** – identifier of the person who granted the permission  
 - **authorizedIdentifier** – identifier of the authorized person or entity  
 - **targetIdentifier** – identifier of the target entity for indirectly granted permissions  
 - **permissionTypes** – list of permission types to search for  
 - **permissionState** – permission status  
 - **queryType** – query type specifying which of the two lists should be returned  

#### Result pagination
The query returns **one page of results** with the number and size specified in the path.
- On the first call, set the parameter `pageOffset = 0`.  
- If another page of results is available, the **`hasMore`** flag will appear in the response.

 - If the login context is composite (NIP-VAT UE), it is possible to retrieve all permissions of administrators and representatives of the entity in the current composite context.  

 Permissions returned by the operation include:  
 - **VatUeManage** – managing permissions within the EU entity  
 - **InvoiceWrite** – issuing invoices  
 - **InvoiceRead** – viewing invoices  
 - **Introspection** – viewing session history  

 The response can be filtered based on the following parameters:  
 - **vatUeIdentifier** – EU entity identifier  
 - **authorizedFingerprintIdentifier** – certificate fingerprint of the authorized person or entity  
 - **permissionTypes** – list of permission types to search for  

#### Result pagination
The query returns **one page of results** with the number and size specified in the path.
- On the first call, set the parameter `pageOffset = 0`.  
- If the next page of results is available, the **`hasMore`** flag will appear in the response.  
- In that case, the query can be called again with the next page number.
 
 > More information:
 > - [Retrieving the list of permissions](https://github.com/CIRFMF/ksef-docs/blob/main/uprawnienia.md#pobranie-listy-uprawnie%C5%84-administrator%C3%B3w-lub-reprezentant%C3%B3w-podmiot%C3%B3w-unijnych-uprawnionych-do-samofakturowania)

**Headers:**

`X-Error-Format: problem-details` - setting this header causes errors to be returned in **Problem Details** format (`application/problem+json`).

**Sorting:**

- startDate (Desc)
- id (Asc)



**Required permissions**: `CredentialsManage`, `CredentialsRead`, `VatUeManage`.

partUploadRequests.description: Data required for the correct upload of individual parts of the invoice batch file. Each part of the batch file declared in fileParts must be uploaded in accordance with the corresponding object in partUploadRequests. The link between the declaration and the upload instruction is the ordinalNumber field. For each part you must: * use the HTTP method indicated in method, * set the address from url, * include the headers from headers, * include the file part content in the request body. `Note: do not add the access token (accessToken) to the headers.` Each part is uploaded in a separate HTTP request. Returned response codes: * 201 – file accepted successfully, * 400 – invalid data, * 401 – invalid authentication, * 403 – no write permission (e.g. upload time has expired).

tags.name: Certificates
tags.description:
A KSeF certificate is a digital proof of identity issued by the KSeF system upon request of an authenticated entity. 
This certificate can be used for:

- authenticating to the KSeF system,
- performing operations in offline mode, including issuing invoices directly in the user's application.

**Note**: Requesting a KSeF certificate is only possible after authentication using a signature (XAdES). Authentication using a KSeF system token does not allow submitting a request.

tags.name: Test data
tags.description:
The API is used to create and manage test data, such as entities, natural persons, and permissions. Entities that can be created include: enforcement authority, VAT group, and local government units. For natural persons, it is possible to specify whether the person is a bailiff. The permission granting and revoking functionality is intended to replicate the behavior of the ZAW-FA form in the test environment.

More information:
- [Test scenarios](https://github.com/CIRFMF/ksef-docs/blob/main/dane-testowe-scenariusze.md)

tags.name: KSeF tokens
tags.description:
A KSeF token is a unique, generated authentication identifier that — on equal terms with a [qualified electronic signature](https://github.com/CIRFMF/ksef-docs/blob/main/uwierzytelnianie.md#21-uwierzytelnianie-kwalifikowanym-podpisem-elektronicznym) — enables [authentication](https://github.com/CIRFMF/ksef-docs/blob/main/uwierzytelnianie.md#22-uwierzytelnianie-tokenem-ksef) to the KSeF API. A KSeF token is issued with an immutable set of permissions defined at the time of its creation; any modification of these permissions requires generating a new token. > **Note!**
> A KSeF token serves as a **confidential authentication secret** — it must be stored exclusively in a trusted and secure vault. More information: - [KSeF token](https://github.com/CIRFMF/ksef-docs/blob/main/tokeny-ksef.md)

tags.name: Gaining access
tags.description:
Authentication in the KSeF API 2.0 system is a mandatory step that must be performed before accessing protected system resources. This process is based on **obtaining an access token** (```accessToken```) in ```JWT``` format, which is then used to authorize API operations.

> More information:
> - [Authentication](https://github.com/CIRFMF/ksef-docs/blob/main/uwierzytelnianie.md)
